title: Palindromes grow from the middle
hook: Count the palindromes hiding in "aaaa". Do you have to test every piece?

knows: two fingers moving apart or together over a list (two-pointers-meet)
what a palindrome is (reads the same backwards)
doesNotKnow: that the palindromes in a string can be counted by growing each centre outward
that a string of n letters has 2n - 1 centres, counting the gaps

misconception: To count palindromic substrings you must test every substring.
objective: The learner can explain that every palindrome is a mirrored stretch around one centre (a letter or a gap), so growing each of the 2n - 1 centres outward until the mirror breaks counts them all once: 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 10 for "aaaa".

claims.text: A palindrome reads the same backwards, so it is a mirrored stretch around a centre: a middle letter (odd length) or a middle gap (even length). Substrings at different positions count separately.
claims.source: Definition of a palindrome and of counting palindromic substrings by (start, end) position, as in the predict question. The odd/even split is a derivation: a substring of odd length has a middle letter, of even length a middle gap. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. Definition; odd-length substrings have a middle letter, even-length a middle gap. Predict question says each start and end position counted separately, matching brute() counting by (i, j).

claims.text: "aaaa" has 10 palindromic substrings: all of its 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 substrings are palindromes. Growing its 7 centres finds 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1 (letter, gap, letter, ...), 10 in all, and every centre stops because the word ends.
claims.source: Demo.tsx grow() over all 7 centres (PER, TOTAL) and brute(); builder's node script (2026-10-14): brute force over all substrings gives 10, centre expansion gives 10 with per-centre counts 1,1,2,2,2,1,1. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. Own node (fc21/pal.mjs): centre counts 1,1,2,2,2,1,1 = 10; every centre stops at the word's end (l < 0 or r = n); brute force 10 = 4+3+2+1 substrings, all palindromes.

claims.text: A string of n letters has 2n - 1 centres (n letters and n - 1 gaps).
claims.source: Each letter is a centre (n) and each gap between neighbouring letters is a centre (n - 1); n + (n - 1) = 2n - 1. For "aaaa", 7. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): VERIFIED. n letters + (n - 1) gaps = 2n - 1; aaaa gives 7 (Demo CENTRES).

claims.text: Each palindrome is found exactly once, from its own middle; each centre grows until the letters differ or the word ends, so a substring whose middle already failed is never tested.
claims.source: Derivation: a palindrome [l, r] is grown only from centre l + r, and growth from that centre reaches [l, r] only through [l+1, r-1], [l+2, r-2], ..., all of which must match first. v2 shows the stop on stage in 'abaa' (red dashed bracket, 'letters differ').

claims.text: In "abaa" the same 7 centres find 6 palindromes (1, 0, 2, 0, 1, 1, 1) and 3 of them stop at a mismatch; the fingers look at 9 of its 10 substrings, and "abaa" itself is never tested because its middle, "ba", fails first.
claims.source: Demo.tsx grow('abaa', k) for k = 0..6; builder's Node run, 2026-10-14: counts 1+0+2+0+1+1+1 = 6, brute force over all 10 substrings also gives 6; fails at centres 1, 3, 4; tested = palindromes + failed comparisons = 6 + 3 = 9; the middle centre (gap 3) fails on [1, 2] = 'ba', so [0, 3] = 'abaa' is never reached.

recall.question: You count the palindromes in a 6-letter word by growing outward from every centre. How many centres do you grow?
recall.why: Every letter is a centre for the odd-length palindromes and every gap between two letters is a centre for the even-length ones: 6 + 5 = 11, which is 2n - 1.
